name: Can Material Price Changes Affect a Written Kitchen Estimate?

mainEntity.name: How should a kitchen remodeling estimate handle material price changes, discontinued products, and supplier delays?
mainEntity.text: How should a kitchen remodeling estimate handle material price changes, discontinued products, and supplier delays?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cabinets, countertops, appliances, fixtures, and tile may change price or availability between estimating and installation. Ask how long the proposal price remains valid and when prices become locked. Confirm whether a deposit locks pricing or only reserves scheduling. The estimate should address discontinued products, backorders, damaged shipments, and supplier-driven increases. Require written approval before substituting a product. The substitution notice should identify the original item, replacement item, quality differences, price adjustment, delivery effect, and warranty implications. Ask whether a lower-cost substitute produces a credit and how that credit is calculated. Confirm who pays for storage, redelivery, or extra labor caused by a supplier problem. To reduce risk, finalize high-cost selections early, retain model numbers and finish names, and request updated pricing before ordering. Compare estimates with the same validity assumptions. A clause that allows unlimited price increases can make the initial total unreliable, while a clearly limited adjustment process provides better budget control. Discuss likely lead-time risks and their effect on the schedule before signing.
acceptedAnswer.description: The estimate should state its price-validity period, ordering deadlines, substitution rules, and responsibility for supplier increases or discontinued products. Require written approval for substitutions and price changes, including any credit for a lower-cost replacement.
